summary: The six filled tapes occur in 14/4, not 14/3
rationale: 14/3 concerns returning from Midyat and the villages. The following verse, 14/4, has 'Əšto šaritat kulle mlalli' and 'Ich habe sechs Tonbänder ganz gefüllt', matching both the words and context of the example.

summary: Repair the corrupted human possessor in the heart-filling example.
rationale: Supplied 8/5 reads lebe du ənsan naša; retain the exact source phrase as replacement, without changing the sense.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (MAC NE Famine/69)

data.turoyo: Məd əzzíwayno ga ko mlele i+ḥreto.
data.translation: When I would go back, he had already filled another one.

rationale: New ko-Preterit box: ko with L-suffixed mlele in repeated anterior-result context; select the second-return token, without repeating the first occurrence.

summary: New box ko-Preterit: example for sense 1 in ko-Preterit (62/245)

data.turoyo: Kal komalyo naqqa ḥreto i ṭaṣayḏi”.
data.translation: Meine Schale hat sich nun gerade aufs Neue gefüllt."

rationale: New Detransitive ko-Preterit box: feminine komalyo with completed filling and renewed current result.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.27/1291)

data.turoyo: Naqla qayəmowa arġalto, mlənwo ab bote kulle maye.
data.translation: Once a rain channel rose, all the houses filled with water.

rationale: First secure Detransitive Preterit-wa: overt houses subject and bare water content. Round 1 left this box unestablished.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.45/1958)

data.turoyo: Hano more du bayto šqiwole ab bote du Sḥaqo d be Šabo, d kətne laxalf di baxča, qayəm aṯiwo maṭro ġalabe, mlowa i dərto maye.
data.translation: This owner of the house had bought Ishaq of the Shabo family’s houses, which are behind the garden; then there had been a lot of rain, the courtyard had filled with water.

rationale: Second Detransitive Preterit-wa example provides feminine mlowa and a complete rain/flood context; contraction remains an editorial question.

summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (Jan 2.4/891)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni šuġlo d tloṯo yawme arbʕo yawme, hway amin, bale kule mloyo mlelan.
data.translation: That is, work of three days, four days, believe me, but we filled all of it right up.

rationale: New active Infinitiv in cognate mloyo mlelan; the reader’s Detransitive classification is not licensed by the active main verb.

summary: New sense 2: (verneint, mit mede) etwas bedeuten, von Belang sein

data.gloss: (verneint, mit mede) etwas bedeuten, von Belang sein

rationale: In haṯi kula lə kməlyo mede the subject is proposed conduct, not a container, and mede expresses its dismissed significance. One clear attestation.

summary: New sense 1: (Detrans.) sich füllen, voll werden; voll sein

data.gloss: (Detrans.) sich füllen, voll werden; voll sein

rationale: Explicitly formulates the already implied sense of the inherited Detransitive boxes; does not replace or renumber any existing labelled sense.

evidence.cite: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/28

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (JL 8.10/1)

data.turoyo: Kətwaylan gubo malyo maye, w ap=pirayḏan azzehən lam=maye.
data.translation: Wir hatten eine Zisterne, (die) voll Wasser (war), und unsere Frauen gingen zum Wasser(holen).

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell: masculine malyo agreeing with gubo, with bare maye content.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 11.11/9)

data.turoyo: W moliwayna ḥlime, ḥeḏər ṣiṭo, aṭ=ṭarfe taxawat hawxa ʕal ḥḏoḏe, maḥtiwaynanne ʕal u=bayto, lo ṭoriwayna mede ftiḥo bayn aṭ=ṭarfani, d u=ʕafro lo=noḥət laltaḥ.
data.translation: Wir füllten die Zweige dick auf, etwa eine Spanne hoch, in Schichten übereinander; wir legten sie auf das Haus und ließen keine offene Stelle zwischen diesen Zweigen, damit die Erde nicht herunterrieseln konnte.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: filling with branches over a roof; material object and support understood.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 11.12/8)

data.turoyo: W məḥyowayno iḏi eba w maydowayno lu=kiso, w bi=zarke gməlyowayno u=kiso, mu=ḥalwawo di=baroše d hawyo gweto, maḥtowaynola bu=kiso.
data.translation: Ich griff mit der Hand hinein und nahm den Beutel, und mit der Schüsssel füllte ich den Beutel mit dieser Milch aus dem Kochtopf, die zu Käse geworden war, ich tat sie in den Beutel.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: container object, m-marked substance and b-instrument in one complete sentence.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JL 11.12/13)

data.turoyo: Hul d u=gḏonayḏi məmle, i=gweto hawxa saymowaynola, w toliwaynala.
data.translation: Bis der Tonkrug sich füllte, machte ich auf diese Weise Käse, und dann hoben wir ihn auf.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell: agentless endpoint under hul d amid habitual preparation.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (JL 12.13/1)

data.turoyo: w ap=pirayḏan-ze ʕal u=gubo molənwa maye.
data.translation: Unsere Frauen waren gerade dabei, an der Zisterne Wasser (in ihre Krüge) zu füllen.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa cell: overt water object with omitted vessel; supports explicit water-drawing gloss.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JL 18.6/9)

data.turoyo: w u=hurkawo, hawxa b iḏoṯan, fətḥinale w gsayminale tannək, w gmolina gawayye ḥašwo komqapṭinale, hanək kəmminanne kutle.
data.translation: und dann öffnen wir diesen (Teig aus) Gries mit unseren Händen und machen ihn dünn, und dann füllen wir das Innere (der Klöße) mit Füllung und schließen sie wieder. Diese (gefüllten Klöße) nennt man kutle.

rationale: Better self-contained Infectum context than inferred water containers: opening, filling and closing dough portions with two bare nominal arguments.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Lahdo The vine press/2)

data.turoyo: w hәnn mәnne ste kito gabayye gubone, čalәkat kәmminanne, mar b ḥamšo hne… me tamo mәmlowiwa w hayo әzzәnwa l ḥa <...>
data.translation: And beside some of them, there were wells, we say holes, say about five um ... They were filled and from there the (squeezed juice) was canalized to another <...>

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum-wa cell: plural collecting hollows fill in the pressing process. Cut before ambiguous maliwo.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (MAC Ishaq Material culture/76)

data.turoyo: Məd‿əmlewalle, msawéwaylan qarʕa bu+ʕafro, di+goro, ṭowo, ʕafro ṣiṭo, ŭ bəṯər maḥtiwa čmənto aʕle, kalšo mawo, čmənto, ŭ hawxa.
data.translation: After they had filled it, they would level its head with soil, the roof’s, well, a span of earth, and later they would put cement on it, lime of this sort, cement, and so forth.

rationale: Thin Preterit-wa cell: completed roof filling anterior to leveling; preserves source form əmlewalle.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (MAC Ishaq Material culture/101)

data.turoyo: disa gmoṭe buqto+ḥreto, buqto yani falqo+ḥreno, buqto, gzobaṭṭe bi+iḏaṯe, gəzzé hawxa hul dməmloyo i+iḏo.
data.translation: once again it would bring another bunch, a bunch, that is, another bit, a bunch, he would grasp them with this hand, he would go like so until his hand gets full.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum cell: accumulating stalks make a body-part container full.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC MuA Quzko/54)

data.turoyo: Səmlan tanuro dlaḥmo ŭ mlay i+xurǧazine laḥmo
data.translation: Make us an oven of bread, and fill up a saddlebag with bread

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: overt saddlebag container and bread content, both zero-marked.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/28)

data.turoyo: Koḥoyər, kalá šk̇afte mliṯo ʕwone.
data.translation: He looks, here’s a cave full of sheep.
data.ref: MAC MuA The Story of Xalaf Agha/28

rationale: Thin Detransitive Part. Pass. cell: clear feminine mliṯo agreement and animate contents.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (MAC NE Interview 2/151)

data.turoyo: B̥anək, ăḷo, iḏan məmlənwa kube hul dmixarǧiwa.
data.translation: Because of those ones, gosh, our hands were filled with thorns until they were inured.

rationale: Thin Detransitive Infectum-wa cell: affected hands as subject and bare thorn content.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (MAC NI death and newlyweds/11)

data.turoyo: Omar, ‘Mlay i+ṣəṭlayḏe <baṣ...> bərġəl w baṣro. Mlaya bərġəl w baṣro, w ṭroṯe u+ruʕyawo, ṭroṯe larke’.
data.translation: He says, ‘Fill the bucket with mea… burgul and meat. Fill it with burgul and meat, and let that shepherd come, let him come here’.

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell: adjacent overt-container Mlay and suffixed-container Mlaya show the alternation in the same instruction.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (PrS 36/14)

data.turoyo: Šaməʕ u Ṣolnas, azzele u kaġad. Maqəmle ʕaskar rabṯo w aṯi, aṯi l bə Zalim, malyo i walaye d Zalim maʕ ʕasekər.
data.translation: Als der Ssôlnâs dies hörte und den Brief empfangen hatte, brach er mit einem grossen Heere auf und kam zu Sâlim. Die Stadt Sâlim's füllte sich mit Truppen.

rationale: Unusual maʕ content marker in eventive Detransitive filling of a town; retain narrative Preterit filing.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (53/107)

data.turoyo: Məqqa d kosaymi, komər: "Haṯi kula lə kməlyo mede. <...>
data.translation: Was sie auch anstellten, er sprach: "All das hat gar nichts zu bedeuten. <...>

rationale: First example of new figurative sense 2: conduct is dismissed as without significance.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (83/82)

data.turoyo: W bu lalyawo i saʕaye traḥsar b lalyo gdomər lan nošayḏe d aʕme, gdomər: “Adlalyo kulxu mlayu ab bawarədaṯxu rṣaṣ w mqaweṣu kulxu b naqla ḥḏo! Lo kolutu hul d moḥutu kulle d aʕmayxu!”
data.translation: In derselben Nacht, um zwölf Uhr, spricht er zu seinen Leuten: "Ladet heute Nacht eure Gewehre mit Blei und schießt sie alle auf einmal ab! Hört nicht auf, ehe ihr alle eure Patronen abgeschossen habt!"

rationale: Thin Imperativ cell and unusual 2pl form; firearm loading uses the ordinary container-plus-content frame.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 1.8/164)

data.turoyo: U Gubo d be Ḥaydari, annaqqa i ʕaskar mlewola, kətwolle dasto mlewolle maye d soḥən.
data.translation: The well of the Ḥaydari family: at that time the soldiers had filled it; they had a basin, they had filled it with water to bathe.

rationale: Round 1 leaves two examples; basin context shows overt water content and two object suffixes.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (Jan 1.8/219)

data.turoyo: Mulena an naʕime du ʕamo bu bayto?!
data.translation: Are we to fill the house with the whole world's children?!

rationale: Unusual contents-object plus b-container frame, rather than a new sense.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.4/927)

data.turoyo: Mlewolən ad dəkoṯanək qalme.
data.translation: Those lice filled the places.

rationale: Animate lice as filling agents with places as object, in the remaining thin active Preterit-wa cell.

summary: Correct 'nsab' to the corpus reading 'ənsan'
rationale: The cited 8/5 reads 'kmole lebe du ənsan naša'. The entry's nsab changes the final consonant n to b and omits part of ənsan; this is beyond clitic or vowel normalization. The same corpus text also has ənsan in 8/20.

summary: Sense 1: revise the gloss
after: füllen, stopfen; (mole maye, mit unausgedrücktem Gefäß) Wasser schöpfen, holen
rationale: Makes the water-drawing use explicit, as supported by the inherited Shabo note and the well contexts; no change to existing numbering.

summary: New idiom: mlele/mole xəneǧər 'mit Dolchstichen durchbohren'

data.turoyo: Mlele xəneǧər, qṭile ʕAṭman.
data.translation: und durchbohrte ihn mit tötlichen Dolchstichen.

rationale: One clear attestation; glossary search xəneǧər found a different verb čkčk, not this collocation. Does not specify number or depth of blows.

summary: New idiom: mle/məmle ʕayno m- '(Detrans.) von jemandes Eigenschaften beeindruckt sein'

data.headword: mle/məmle ʕayno m- '(Detrans.) von jemandes Eigenschaften beeindruckt sein'
data.turoyo: Madam ki u gawrano hat, u farəsano hat, mle ʕayni menux mi gawruṯayḏux. Waʕd ʕam aloho gdəṯyono aʕmux.
data.translation: Da du ein solcher Mann, ein solcher Ritter bist, und mein Auge von dir, von deiner Mannhaftigkeit erfüllt ist, gelobe ich Gott, daß ich mit dir kommen werde.

rationale: Already repeated in inherited filling examples; search ʕayna confirms it there but no separate idiom. Add an explicit collocation listing without moving inherited examples.

summary: New idiom: mlele/mole u šarwolo 'sich die Hose vollmachen'

data.headword: mlele/mole u šarwolo 'sich die Hose vollmachen'
data.turoyo: W hiye mlele u šarwolo, maz zuḥṯe lo koḏəʕ, ayko kəzze.
data.translation: Er aber machte die Hose voll und wußte vor Angst nicht, wohin die Reise ging.

rationale: Glossary search šarwolo found no mly idiom; 56/59 confirms the same soiling scene.

summary: New idiom: lebo malyo m- '(Detrans.) auf jemanden zornig sein'

data.headword: lebo malyo m- '(Detrans.) auf jemanden zornig sein'
data.turoyo: Komər hano u aḥuno yo, lebe malyo mine yo, griš (+det) me qume.
data.translation: Jener, der Bruder, war sehr zornig auf ihn. Er ritt vor ihm weg.

rationale: Search malyo found overt anger fullness under mly but no human-target grudge idiom. One attestation; duration is not specified.

summary: New idiom: mlele/mole dukṯo + poss. 'jemandes Stelle einnehmen, etwas ersetzen'

data.headword: mlele/mole dukṯo + poss. 'jemandes Stelle einnehmen, etwas ersetzen'
data.turoyo: Ninorta: Əno laǧani, xabro d aṯro ḥubo mqadašto yo. Layt mede ste bi briṯaṯe d qodər mole dukṯa, yaʕni di ḥubaṯe.
data.translation: Ninorta: For me, the word homeland is a sacred love. There is nothing else in this world that can fill its place, that is, the place of this love.

rationale: One attestation: an abstract love cannot be spatially occupied; dukṯa refers back to ḥubo. Checked supplied entry, round 1 idioms, and glossary searches dukṯ and mole duk; no matching mly collocation found.

summary: Detransitive sense 1 is newly formulated for an already established section, not a newly discovered meaning. Distinguish eventive mle/malyo with a filled subject, Infectum məmle, and agreeing Part. Pass. malyo/malye/mliṯo. Gender and syntax matter: malyo may be feminine finite in town-filling but masculine agreeing with gubo in JL 8.10/1.

Active filling alternates between container object plus contents, and contents object plus container goal. Instruments b-, substances m-, bare two-NP frames, and contents ellipsis coexist. Roofs and cooking mixtures do not independently establish new senses.

ko mlele in MAC NE Famine/69 and komalyo in 62/245 warrant active and Detransitive ko-Preterit boxes respectively. Ambiguous maliwo, malənwa and maliwa do not securely establish a Detransitive Preterit-wa box.

Emotional heart filling is inherited; the eye-admiration, dagger, trouser and human-target heart collocations are now explicitly listed. Cassette recording already has an idiom and is not added again.

Old prs references are edition page/line style, whereas current PrS references are text/verse: PrS 12/8 corresponds to prs 27/32, PrS 12/24 to prs 28/21, and PrS 81/16 to prs 255/31. These are not citation errors merely because the numbers differ.
The explicitly Classical Syriac malyaṯ burkoṯo at 66/279 is excluded from Turoyo morphology; unclear clothing mloye at PrS 87/6 is not accepted as verbal evidence.

Round 1 already formulates Detransitive sense 1 and fills the ordinary Infectum, Infectum-wa and Part. Pass. cells to four or five. Jan nominal containers of culture, emotional heart/mouth fullness, libraries and crowds continue that meaning; do not duplicate round 1 senses or collocations.

mlənwo with houses subject (Jan 1.27/1291) supplies the Detransitive Preterit-wa evidence round 1 lacked. Feminine mlowa in a rain context is grouped provisionally. By contrast mliṯo wa at Jan 2.10/2147 is Part. Pass. plus copula, not a new finite box.

The agentless Detransitive construction also describes a commanded filling task at Jan 2.4/884: the soldiers are pragmatically responsible, while the pit remains the grammatical subject. Detransitive is not restricted to spontaneous accumulation.
The cognate mloyo mlelan (Jan 2.4/891) belongs with active filling, not a Detransitive Infinitiv inferred from an action-noun shape.

Six supplied compact records lack verse_turoyo: Jan 1.8/241, 1.46/2034, 2.4/504, 2.4/891 (mlelan), 2.4/896 and 2.35/5528. The mlelan token at 2.4/891 is independently visible in the full companion mloyo record; the other five cannot be independently checked from this input. They remain no_add with that limitation, not invented source text.

mulanwola at Jan 1.59/2901 fits the surrounding third-person procedural series maḥtiwo/ubiwo; the reader’s first-person plural claim is not secure. mlanwolle/mlanwo at Jan 2.26/4399 may instead be reduced Infectum-wa; no box example is selected from that ambiguous pair.
Jan English is the project machine translation, not an edition translation. It is reproduced only as supplied and is not evidence for senses; all semantic decisions rest on the Turoyo.

Resolve maliwo (Lahdo The vine press/2), malənwa (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/59), maliwa (MAC Murder in Kfarze, The Testimony of Farida/99), and məlyowa (JTM 2.4/2): finite event, filled-state predicate, or active use? These were withheld from form additions.
Check mloye in PrS 87/6 against the edition and a speaker; is it verbal at all?
Confirm segmentation and agreement in Mlalle/Mlallalle, including MAC NE Story of Joseph/18, PrS 12/3, 48/51, and the apparent gender mismatches in MAC NE Old woman and a fox/24 and 67/168.
Does dagger filling entail repeated blows or full penetration? What substance is implied by the trouser-soiling euphemism? Neither is specified in the new glosses.
Confirm whether lebe malyo mine implies enduring resentment or simply anger in 57/228; current gloss avoids duration.
Verify source reading du ənsan naša at 8/5 and the supplied 14/4 verse boundary before accepting those existing-material corrections.
Confirm mlowa at Jan 1.45/1958 as contracted Detransitive Preterit-wa; distinguish məlyowa at Jan 1.40/1776 from a past filled-state predicate.
Confirm the active cognate Infinitiv mloyo at Jan 2.4/891 and its paradigm.
Supply the five missing full verses for compact records listed above; no source reconstruction has been attempted.
At Jan 1.16/698, does feminine məmloyo take fire as subject (spreading/accumulating), contrasting with the kiln as subject of preceding məmle?
Confirm person and agent/object segmentation of mulanwola (Jan 1.59/2901), mlanwolle/mlanwo (Jan 2.26/4399), and whether mlewola/mlewolle at Jan 1.8/164 both refer to the basin.

Filled spaces include roof frameworks, food mixtures, the space before the chest, wounds and firearms; contents may be zero-marked or m-marked, while a container may be the direct object or a b-/ʕal-marked goal.
Detransitive fullness extends to open alleys, a palace containing animals, a loaded ant and occupied hours. These alter the filled participant or contents, not the core fullness meaning.

Contents may be a bare object and container a b-goal, including children in a house, juice in tins and preserved meat in skins/jars. These instantiate the filling alternation already described in round 1.
Abstract needs/emptiness are filled by parents through education. Given inherited heart-filling, retain this participant extension without a separate numbered sense.
Detransitive temporal fullness: məlyowa i məddaṯṯe describes a completed allotted term. Record a temporal extension; finite event versus filled-state predication is unresolved.
